title: A comparative study of two intrastromal corneal ring segment models in keratoconus: A retrospective study

groups.description: Group 1: 39 eyes with moderate-to-advanced keratoconus (patients aged 18-40 years, cross-linked at least 6 months earlier without progression) receiving femtosecond-assisted BioRing intrastromal ring segments (Methods, Table 1)

Group 2: 35 eyes with moderate-to-advanced keratoconus (patients aged 18-40 years, cross-linked at least 6 months earlier without progression) receiving femtosecond-assisted Keraring intrastromal ring segments (Methods, Table 1)

series.notes: mean ± SD; anterior Kmax from Sirius Plus tomography (Methods)
mean ± SD; anterior Kmax from Sirius Plus tomography (Methods)

exclusions.what: PMC12448536.xml::IJO.IJO_14_25-T4!R4 (Kmax of moderate and advanced sub-groups of each group)
exclusions.reason: stage sub-groups give the 6-month postoperative Kmax only, without their baseline Kmax; not admissible, so the whole groups (Table 2) are extracted and no eye is counted twice

notes: Every eligible eye had cross-linking at least 6 months before ring implantation without progression; the tabulated follow-up starts at ring implantation, so the context is ring segments alone (icrs).
Both groups are commercially available ring-segment models chosen by the patients (cost); no investigational arm is declared, so both roles are control.
Age group mixed: the inclusion range 18-40 years includes 18-year-olds, whom the protocol counts as paediatric.
Table 1 labels the group sizes 'Number of patients' but the Methods give them as eyes (74 eyes of 58 patients); n is the number of eyes. Missing data were excluded (Methods).

Tomography only preoperatively and at 6 months. K1 and K2 (anterior and posterior), thickness, symmetry and vertex indices, RMS, HOA (Table 2), visual acuity and refraction (Tables 1, 4) are tabulated and not used.
